title: Ehrhart polynomials for 3D lattice polytopes generalizing Pick's formula

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Cross-polytope Ehrhart theory formalized with 69 proved theorems across 695 lines. Covers Ehrhart polynomials, reciprocity, h*-vectors, reflexivity, duality, and dimension recurrence for the hyperoctahedron family.

Cross-polytope Ehrhart polynomials: β₁ L(n)=2n+1, β₂ L(n)=2n²+2n+1, β₃ L(n)=(4/3)n³+2n²+(8/3)n+1
Interior polynomials with shift property L*(n) = L(n-1)
Monotonicity, boundary counts, volume products, binomial expansion
insights: Cross-polytope h*-polynomial is (1+z)^d - binomial coefficients as h*-vector entries
Interior shift property: L*(n) = L(n-1) holds for all cross-polytopes (simplicial + reflexive)
Cross-polytope β_d is dual to cube □_d; self-dual in 1D, distinct in higher dimensions
Boundary of β_d at n=1 has exactly 2d points (the vertices ±e_i)
Volume product vol(β_d)·vol(□_d) = 4^d/d\! connects dual polytopes
Cross-polytope Ehrhart satisfies dimension recurrence from lower-dimensional counts
All cross-polytope h*-vectors are palindromic, confirming reflexivity (Hibi theorem)
